findings.issue_text: [High/concurrency] Backup-code consumption is a read-modify-write without a transaction or conditional update, allowing concurrent logins to accept the same code or overwrite each other’s changes and restore a consumed code.

[Medium/bug] 2FA is enabled on the server before backup codes are shown, but onEnable() runs only through the custom Close button, so Escape, overlay dismissal, or the built-in close control leaves the parent UI stale while 2FA is active.

[Medium/bug] The UI reports that backup codes were copied without awaiting or handling navigator.clipboard.writeText, so clipboard denial or unavailability can lead users to close the only code display believing the codes were saved.
[Medium/test_gap] The tests verify only the backup-code download filename and toast appearance, not that a backup code authenticates, is rejected after use, or authorizes disabling 2FA.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] 2FA is enabled on the server before backup codes are shown, but onEnable() runs only through the custom Close button, so Escape, overlay dismissal, or the built-in close control leaves the parent UI stale while 2FA is active.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, when the TOTP code is verified successfully (response.status === 200 in handleEnable), it sets step to SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes (line 132). The 2FA is already enabled on the server at this point. However, onEnable() is only called when the user clicks the 'Close' button (line 268-272). The Dialog component likely has other ways to close (Escape key, clicking overlay, built-in close button) that would bypass onEnable(). This means the parent component's state wouldn't be updated to reflect that 2FA is now enabled, causing UI inconsistency. The diff shows onOpenChange is passed to Dialog but there's no handling to call onEnable() when the dialog closes through other means during the DisplayBackupCodes step.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] The UI reports that backup codes were copied without awaiting or handling navigator.clipboard.writeText, so clipboard denial or unavailability can lead users to close the only code display believing the codes were saved.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx that the copy button handler calls navigator.clipboard.writeText() without awaiting it, then immediately shows a success toast. If the clipboard API fails (permission denied, unavailable, etc.), the user sees 'Backup codes copied!' but nothing was actually copied. Since backup codes are shown only once and users may close the dialog believing they saved the codes, this is a real bug that could lead to users losing access to their 2FA recovery codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] The tests verify only the backup-code download filename and toast appearance, not that a backup code authenticates, is rejected after use, or authorizes disabling 2FA.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds significant backup code functionality: login authentication with backup codes (next-auth-options.ts lines 128-160), disabling 2FA with backup codes (disable.ts lines 46-72), and backup code generation/display (setup.ts, EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx). The test file login.2fa.e2e.ts only tests downloading and copying backup codes (lines 110-125), with a TODO comment on line 12 explicitly acknowledging 'add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup'. This is a legitimate gap - new security-critical authentication logic lacks test coverage for its core functionality.
